selected_mechanism.definition: A Science and Technology Center cooperative agreement funds a lead university in annual, reviewed increments while preserving active NSF oversight of a multi-institution research center.

chokepoint.binary_decision: Submit the annual project report on time so NSF can review and process future funding increments, or fail to submit it and delay that processing.
chokepoint.why_asymmetric: The public headline presents a five-year award, but the award record shows one fiscal-year obligation. NSF makes each year contingent on satisfactory annual review, and its rules make the principal investigator's report a necessary input. Without that filing, future increment processing is delayed before any public account of center results can matter.

selected_mechanism.texas_consequence: UT Austin receives the federal cooperative agreement as the lead institution, controls the center budget and partner subawards, and hosts part of the real-world HERO Facility Network. The official award record lists $29,999,998 as the estimated total and $5,999,999 as obligated for fiscal year 2026.
selected_mechanism.structural_read: The vehicle gives Austin meaningful control over a national AI and robotics network while keeping future federal increments tied to annual evidence. That is a stronger structure than an unrestricted five-year transfer, but it means the useful public measure is obligations and performance review, not the headline total.
selected_mechanism.forward_implication: The next useful public check is an amendment to the NSF award record showing another funding increment, paired with whatever management indicators UT makes available from the first annual review.

verified_facts.claim: NSF announced the Center for Human and Robot Co-Adaptation on August 26th, 2026, with UT Austin as lead.
NSF award 2535195 is a cooperative agreement with an estimated total of $29,999,998 and $5,999,999 obligated for fiscal year 2026.
The solicitation makes the lead institution responsible for overall management, the budget, and oversight of partner subawards.
The Center Director manages staffing and resource allocation and serves as liaison with NSF.

The principal investigator must submit an annual project report no later than 90 days before the end of the current budget period. Missing reports delay review and processing of future funding increments.
Each year of STC support is contingent on satisfactory annual review, and NSF uses reports, site visits, and management indicators to determine continued funding level.
